text.p: French glass maker Saint-Gobain has the means to carry on its acquisitions policy without putting profit growth in jeopardy, chairman Jean-Louis Beffa said on Monday.

"As our debt stands at 30 percent of capital and having already paid off half the Poliet acquisition, the group has the financial means to pursue a dynamic acquisitions strategy, while keeping an eye open for opportunities and staying committed to the growth of net earnings per share", he said in an interview with business newspaper Les Echos.

He added that with a 100-billion-franc turnover, "Saint-Gobain is heading toward cashflow of between 11 to 12 billion francs, six to seven billion francs of investment, and four to five billion net profit."
"It can pay shareholders, reduce its debt and consider further acquisitions," he added.
In 1995, the group posted net profit of 4.2 billion francs.
